claim: For CloudFront, API Gateway, Amazon Cognito, App Runner and Verified Access, the AWS WAF body inspection limit is 16 KB by default and can be raised in 16 KB increments up to 64 KB.
question: What is the default AWS WAF body inspection limit for CloudFront and API Gateway, and how high can it go?

qualifiers.scope: per web ACL association, for CloudFront, API Gateway, Cognito, App Runner and Verified Access
qualifiers.condition: set in the web ACL's resource association configuration; the options are 16, 32, 48 and 64 KB

evidence.quote: For CloudFront, API Gateway, Amazon Cognito, App Runner, Verified Access, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, the default limit is 16 KB (16,384 bytes), and you can increase the limit for any of the resource types by increments of 16 KB, up to 64 KB.
| Maximum size of a web request body that can be inspected for CloudFront, API Gateway, Amazon Cognito, App Runner, Verified Access, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway protections\*\* | 64 KB |
evidence.table_header: | Resource | Quota per account per Region |

note: The quotas page lists Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway both at 16 KB maximum (own row) and in the 64 KB row; the claim leaves AgentCore out.

claim: When you raise the body inspection limit, you pay extra only for requests whose bodies are larger than the default 16 KB: $0.30 per million requests for each additional 16KB analyzed.
question: What does it cost to inspect request bodies larger than the default AWS WAF limit?

qualifiers.scope: per web ACL, for CloudFront, API Gateway, Cognito, App Runner and Verified Access
qualifiers.condition: list price on the AWS WAF pricing page; prices may vary across AWS Regions

evidence.quote: You're charged extra only for the inspection of requests that have body sizes larger than the default 16 KB.
In addition, you will be charged $0.30 per million requests for each additional 16KB analyzed beyond the default body inspection limit.

claim: Each rule that you add to a web ACL costs $1.00 per month, and each rule group or managed rule group that you add also costs $1.00 per month (prorated hourly).

claim: On November 18, 2025, CloudFront distributions associated with AWS WAF became eligible for flat-rate pricing plans, which have preset service quotas and give no unexpected usage charges for that distribution.
question: What did CloudFront flat-rate pricing plans change for AWS WAF, and when?

evidence.quote: | [AWS WAF integration with CloudFront flat-rate pricing plans](cloudfront-features.md) | You can now subscribe CloudFront distributions associated with AWS WAF to a flat-rate pricing plan. This new pricing plan is different from pay-as-you-go pricing in that pricing plans have preset service quotas for usage and resources. Once you subscribe a distribution for a pricing plan, you won't receive unexpected usage charges for that distribution. You will have a single price for all resources and features that are included in the pricing plan.  | November 18, 2025 |

The flat-rate plans, available with Amazon CloudFront, combine global content delivery with AWS WAF, DDoS protection, Amazon Route 53 DNS, Amazon CloudWatch Logs ingestion, and serverless edge compute into a simple monthly price with no overage charges.
